results.wikipedia_summary: Scrophularia umbrosa, the green figwort, water betony, or water figwort, is a perennial herbaceous plant found in temperate regions of the Northern hemisphere except western North America. Synonyms are Scrophularia alata Gilib.; Scrophularia ehrharti Stevens; Scrophularia hurstii Druce; Scrophularia towndrowi Druce. It grows in moist and cultivated waste ground.

results.wikipedia_summary: Carex divulsa, the grey sedge, is a species of flowering plant in the genus Carex, native to Macaronesia, Europe, northwest Africa, the Caucasus region, and the Middle East as far east as Turkmenistan. It has been introduced to northeast Argentina, the District of Columbia and Pennsylvania in the United States, Ontario in Canada, the North Island of New Zealand, and Tasmania and Victoria in Australia. It is the namesake of the Carex divulsa aggregate.

conservation_status.description: Exaculum pusillum has a restricted distribution (area of occupancy of less than 2,000 km2) and it is rare throughout most of its range. But the populations are not severely fragmented and it is found at more than ten locations. The current population trends are not known, but it is presumed to be experiencing a decline in population size due to the threats to its wetland habitat. It is therefore listed as Near Threatened.
